### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/auth/admin/* (route, a path literal in a comment in actions))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db0ab0efd8e40fab3c74c015bf3b1446ee99af33` — the merge of head `9d6dba495fe8727febe113a7252bac82e99ed10f` into base `bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db0ab0efd8e40fab3c74c015bf3b1446ee99af33 && git checkout db0ab0efd8e40fab3c74c015bf3b1446ee99af33
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 9d6dba495fe8727febe113a7252bac82e99ed10f && git checkout -B drift-repro bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 && git merge --no-ff 9d6dba495fe8727febe113a7252bac82e99ed10f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8631da39e567beadd0b908f03c77a6faa9197138`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts

Inputs read: card #33759 with its Claim (6896010564) and os-dev-report (6896885009); this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main`; the check-runs on the head (58 success, 13 skipped, none failed, none pending when this record was written). The four remaining files (two test files, `platform-objects.test.ts`, the changeset) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read only to judge the two files above.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`sys_user.ban_user` / `unban_user` lose the lowered `&& features.admin == true` conjunct.** Right. The parsed `visible` is now the authored predicate alone (standing, then the row's `banned` state); `requiredPermissions`, `target`, `recordIdParam`, params and `ai` are byte-identical. The offer set widens to every kernel serving `features.admin` false, which `auth-manager.ts` computes as `pluginConfig.admin ?? resolveScimEnabled(pluginConfig)`.
2. **No accept set moves.** Right. `ActionSchema` is untouched, `requiresFeature` stays authorable with the same vocabulary, and no door changes: the diff holds no server file.
3. **`PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin.gatedInputs` goes from six booked paths to four.** Right, and forced: `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` walks registry to objects (a booked path must carry the gate as a conjunct) and objects to registry, so the two edits can only land together. Export name, kind and declared entry shape (`PublicAuthFeatureEntry`) are unchanged; `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json` records `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES (const)` and is not in the diff, and the `Type Check` lanes that carry `check:api-surface` and `check:generated` are green on the head.
4. **Server-side exposure is unchanged.** Right. `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` hold no `features` read at the head; the action door and MCP `list_actions` judge `requiredPermissions` (`platform-admin-action-gate.ts`), which this diff leaves alone. Only the console's offer changes.
5. **The four remaining admin actions keep the gate.** Right. `unlock_user`, `create_user`, `set_user_password`, `impersonate_user` still carry `requiresFeature: 'admin'`, and the new CONTROL roster pins that exact list.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — upheld; see ③ for the open question on the spec half.

The changeset names `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/spec`, both `patch`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. That matches what the diff publishes: a behaviour fix in one package and a registry value in the other, no key an author can write added, removed or re-meant, so `none` and therefore `patch` on each moved package. `Check Changeset` is green. The spec line is owed, not optional: the registry constant ships in `@objectstack/spec/kernel`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_question (Clause-② for the spec half, literal tuple type loses two members): answer A, keep `Clause-②: no`.** Reasons, each read in the tree:
  - The contract an entry declares is `PublicAuthFeatureEntry`, where `gatedInputs` is `readonly string[]`, optional; `as const satisfies` holds every entry to it. Membership of that array is the registry's data, not its surface: the file's own header calls it a classification registry held in lockstep by CI guards, and it changes whenever an input gains or loses a gate.
  - The repository's instrument for the public surface, `api-surface/kernel.json`, snapshots name and kind, and it does not move.
  - The readers at the head are the two lockstep guards (`spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.test.ts`, `platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts`); the second already reads the field through a `readonly string[]` cast. `Type Check UI`, which compiles the Console against this PR's spec, is green, so nothing under `ui/` depended on the two literals.
  - Read against the narrowing face's own question (does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's refusal real?): neither. The removal records that two inputs are offered in MORE places.
  - Residual, stated so it is not lost: a consumer outside this repository that typed against the two literal members (an index past 3, or the literal passed to `includes` on the uncast tuple) would stop compiling. No such reader exists here, and the dev's measurement and mine agree; this is not enough to make the PR a breaking narrowing.
- **Deviation, file surface widened by two forced edits** (`public-auth-features.ts`, `platform-objects.test.ts`): accepted. Both are forced by the lockstep in ① 3 and are named in the PR body; the spec edit is what brings this PR to the contract tier, correctly.
- **Deviation, suites and ablations on a1fd3723, head 8631da39 adds only the changeset's spec line**: accepted. The net diff confirms the changeset is the only file that could differ, and the head's own check-runs are green.
- **Deviation, first ablation was a refused no-op**: accepted as declared; no reading was taken from it.
- **Deviation, PR-body slip** ("Root changeset: `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch" while the changeset also carries `@objectstack/spec`): confirmed, see N4.
- **out_of_scope_finding (`unlock_user` keeps the gate while its door looks unconditional)**: confirmed as a real open measurement, not a defect of this PR. `auth-plugin.ts` mounts `admin/unlock-user` with no plugin condition, and `sys-user-set-manager-action.test.ts` says so in prose. The card's ask is explicit that every other admin action stays as it is, so leaving it is right. It needs its own card: measure whether `unlock-user` works with the plugin off, then keep or drop the gate. See N1 for the sentence in this diff that touches it.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`** (hits). Holds against the card and against its first consumer. The inline comment's two claims were read in the cited code: the doors are ObjectStack mounts (`auth-plugin.ts`, the `admin/ban-user` and `admin/unban-user` routes sit in an unconditional block beside `admin/create-user`), and they work without the vendor plugin (`getBanWriter` returns the data-engine writer when `isAdminPluginMounted()` is false; `user-session-admission.ts` refuses a banned row `403 BANNED_USER` when the plugin is not mounted and lifts an expired ban as the vendor does). The `gatedInputs XOR exempt` rule still holds for `admin` (four paths remain), and the path grammar test is unaffected.

**`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`** (implementing). Agrees with the contract, sentence by sentence, for the two actions. Attempts to break it:

- *The row predicate on a plugin-off kernel.* `banned`, `ban_reason` and `ban_expires` are declared on `sys_user` unconditionally (`banned` with `defaultValue: false`, and in the default list columns), so `has(record.banned)` does not silently hide both buttons where the vendor plugin never added its columns.
- *The flag and the mount can disagree.* `plugins.admin: false` with SCIM on serves `features.admin` false while the vendor plugin is mounted. The door picks its writer from the built instance, not from the flag, so the action works on either side of that disagreement.
- *A member, or an org admin, on a plugin-off kernel.* The standing leg is untouched and the door runs `gateAdmin` first; the new tests pin the standing leg with the plugin off.
- *A managed environment.* The host seam may refuse a deactivation (an organization owner or admin `409`, a host fault `503`); the button is offered and the door answers the host's refusal. That is the behaviour #33227 shipped and the card names managed environments as in scope.
- *AI exposure.* ① 4.

The live pin is the right shape for the claim: it reads the DECLARED action's `visible`, `target`, `recordIdParam` and params, evaluates the offer under the features that kernel actually serves, and drives the real door through to a refused sign-in and back. The CONTROL is not vacuous: it derives the gated roster from the parsed object and expects exactly the four names.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — the rewritten block header in `sys-user.object.ts` keeps the rationale "the UI hides them instead of rendering buttons that 404" and now attaches it by name to `unlock_user` and `create_user`. For `unlock_user` the tree does not support it (unconditional mount, above). The gate itself is out of this card's scope; the sentence would be truer as "gated on the admin plugin" without the 404 claim for `unlock_user`. Leave as an accepted deviation and carry it into the `unlock_user` card.
- N2 (nit) — the same header still says `banned` "stays true past `ban_expires` until better-auth clears it at the user's next sign-in". On the kernels this PR newly reaches, `user-session-admission.ts` clears it, not better-auth. Display reasoning is unchanged. The header rewording also orphans a verbatim quote in `sys-user-set-manager-action.test.ts` ("only wired when `auth.plugins.admin` is enabled"), which no longer appears in the header.
- N3 (nit, follow-up card, outside the diff) — two published texts still teach that `ban-user` needs the admin plugin, and this PR makes the first-party action contradict both: `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` uses `ban_user` with `requiresFeature: admin` as the worked example of the sugar ("Hidden entirely when the admin plugin is off (instead of a button that 404s)"), and `AuthFamiliesSchema.admin` in `packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts` lists `ban-user` in the family whose routes "answer a plain 404" when the flag is false. The second has been untrue since #33227. The Docs Drift Check on this PR listed `approvals.mdx` and missed the first. Neither is in the diff; the doc example wants another action (`impersonate_user` fits), and the `describe()` wants `ban-user` taken out of its list (a `check:docs` regeneration).
- N4 (nit, prose faces) — the PR body's "Root changeset" bullet omits `@objectstack/spec`; and the `Clause-②:` line, in the body and in the changeset, still ends with the dispatch-time clause "the dev measures the gaining kernels and the seat amends if the diff reads otherwise", which will ship in two `CHANGELOG.md` files. The measurement is done and the answer is `no`; the body can be fixed without moving the head, the changeset copy is an accepted deviation unless the seat chooses to move the head for it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9d6dba495fe8727febe113a7252bac82e99ed10f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts + packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts

Inputs read: card #33759 with its Claim (6896010564) and os-dev-report (6896885009); this PR's body, file list, comments and net diff against `main` at this head; the check-runs on this head. This head is a merge of `main` (`bc6b7ffd`) into `8631da39`; the earlier record 6897296837 on `8631da39` was read as an input and every judgment below was re-made on this head's tree. The net diff against `main` is the same six files with the same hunks as on `8631da39`. The four files outside Scope (two test files, `platform-objects.test.ts`, the changeset) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read only to judge the two files in Scope.

Check-runs on this head when this record was written: 67 runs, all concluded: 56 `success`, 11 `skipped`, none failed, none pending. Among the successes: `Check Changeset`, the four `Type Check` lanes and `Type Check UI`, `Build Core`, the `Lint` lanes, `Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8 (the shards that carry the lockstep guard, the lowering matrix and the two new pins), `Test UI` 1/16 to 16/16, `Live E2E UI`, `Spec property liveness` and `Dogfood Regression Gate`. The skipped runs are opt-in or path-filtered lanes (`Build Docs`, `Lint UI`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Temporal Conformance`, the 18.x upgrade harness, the packed-tarball smoke, the queue-verdict and schedule lanes).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`sys_user.ban_user` and `unban_user` lose the lowered `features.admin == true` conjunct.** Right. Each action's parsed `visible` is now its authored predicate alone (the platform-admin standing, then the row's `banned` state). `target`, `requiredPermissions`, `recordIdParam`, params and `ai` are untouched by the diff. The offer widens to every kernel that serves `features.admin` false, which `auth-manager.ts` computes as `pluginConfig.admin ?? resolveScimEnabled(pluginConfig)`: a self-hosted kernel on the default config and a managed Free or Team environment.
2. **No accept set moves.** Right. `ActionSchema` is not in the diff, `requiresFeature` stays authorable with the same flag vocabulary, and the diff holds no server file, so no door accepts or refuses anything new.
3. **`PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin.gatedInputs` goes from six booked paths to four.** Right, and forced. `feature-gate-guard.test.ts` walks registry to objects (a booked path must carry the gate as a top-level conjunct) and objects to registry, so the registry edit and the two `requiresFeature` removals can only land together. The export keeps its name, its kind and its entry type `PublicAuthFeatureEntry`; `packages/spec/api-surface/kernel.json` lists `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES (const)` and is not in the diff.
4. **The four other admin actions keep the gate.** Right. `unlock_user`, `create_user`, `set_user_password` and `impersonate_user` still carry `requiresFeature: 'admin'` at this head, and stay booked.
5. **Nothing server-side reads the offer.** Right. The two doors run `gateAdmin` first whatever `visible` says; the block header's own sentence, "no door reads `visible`", holds for both mounts in `auth-plugin.ts`.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — upheld. Offering two existing actions on more kernels widens no accepted input and removes no declared capability; the spec half is answered under ③.

The changeset names `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@objectstack/spec`, both `patch`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. That matches what the diff publishes: a console-offer fix in one package and a registry value in the other, with no authorable key added, removed or re-meant. The spec line is owed, because the registry constant ships in `@objectstack/spec/kernel`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_question (spec half: the `as const` tuple type of `admin.gatedInputs` loses two literal members): answer A, keep `Clause-②: no`.** The declared contract of an entry is `PublicAuthFeatureEntry`, where `gatedInputs` is an optional `readonly string[]`; the registry is held to it by `satisfies`. Which paths the array holds is the registry's data, and the file's header describes it as a classification registry kept in lockstep by CI guards. Readers of `gatedInputs` at this head are `spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.test.ts` and `platform-objects/src/feature-gate-guard.test.ts`, plus a comment in `sys-user-set-manager-action.test.ts` and two `test-typecheck-debt.json` ledgers; no runtime or `ui/` reader. Residual, stated so it is not lost: a consumer outside this repository that typed against the two removed literals would stop compiling. That does not make the change a narrowing of a declared capability.
- **Deviation, file surface widened by two forced edits** (`public-auth-features.ts`, `platform-objects.test.ts`): accepted. Both follow from ① 3 and both are named in the PR body. The spec edit is what puts this PR on the schema face.
- **Deviation, suites and ablations ran on `a1fd3723`, derived gates on `8631da39`**: accepted for those heads. Neither is this head; this head's evidence is its own check-runs, reported above.
- **Deviation, first ablation was a refused no-op**: accepted as declared; no reading was taken from it.
- **Deviation, PR-body slip on the changeset bullet**: closed on the prose face. The body now reads "`@objectstack/platform-objects` patch and `@objectstack/spec` patch".
- **out_of_scope_finding (`unlock_user` keeps the gate while its door is mounted unconditionally)**: confirmed as an open measurement and not a defect of this PR. `auth-plugin.ts` mounts `admin/unlock-user` with no plugin condition, and the card asks that every other admin action stay as it is. The seat's comment 6897338167 carries it to #34010.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`** (hits). The change holds against the card and against its first consumer, the lockstep guard. The new comment makes two claims, both read in the cited code at this head:

- "their doors are ObjectStack mounts": `auth-plugin.ts` registers `admin/ban-user` and `admin/unban-user` in a bare block beside `admin/create-user`, under no plugin condition.
- "that work without the admin plugin": `getBanWriter` returns the data-engine writer when `isAdminPluginMounted()` is false, and `isAdminPluginMounted()` asks the built instance for its `banUser` endpoint. `refuseInactiveUserSession` in `user-session-admission.ts` then refuses a banned row with `FORBIDDEN` and code `BANNED_USER`, only when the plugin is not mounted (`enforceBan` in `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts`).

The rule "`gatedInputs` or `exempt`, never both and never neither" still holds for `admin`: four paths remain. The `cloudManaged` entry books neither action, so a managed kernel hides neither through that flag.

**`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`** (implementing). The code agrees with the contract for the two actions. Attempts to break it:

- *The row predicate on a kernel whose better-auth user model has no ban fields.* `banned`, `ban_reason` and `ban_expires` are fields of `sys_user` itself, declared unconditionally, `banned` with `defaultValue: false`. The existing truth table in `action-state-visibility.test.ts` covers a `null` `banned` as not banned, so Ban is offered on a row the vendor never wrote the column for.
- *The flag and the mount disagreeing.* `plugins.admin: false` with SCIM effective is refused at construction (`assertScimAdminCoherence`), so the served flag and the plugin list come from one expression. If the plugin failed to mount while the flag reads true, the door still picks its writer from the built instance, so the action works either way.
- *A caller without the standing.* The standing leg of both predicates is untouched, `requiredPermissions` still carries `PLATFORM_ADMIN_USERS_GATE`, and the door answers any other caller a refusal before reading the body.
- *An expired ban on a plugin-off kernel.* `refuseInactiveUserSession` lifts it and admits the session, as the vendor does, so Unban on a row that still reads banned stays harmless.
- *A managed environment.* With an environment-user host wired, a deactivation may be refused by the host (an organization owner or admin) or refused when the host does not answer; the button is offered and the door carries the host's answer. The card names managed environments as in scope.
- *The action's own promise.* The `description` says the banned person is signed out; `runAdminBanUser` calls `deleteUserSessions` after the write on either writer.

The block header's new paragraph was read sentence by sentence against the same code and holds. The remaining findings are nits; none changes correctness or the contract.

- N1 (nit) — the rewritten header keeps "the UI hides them instead of rendering buttons that 404" and now attaches it by name to `unlock_user` and `create_user`. Both doors are ObjectStack mounts registered without a plugin condition, so a plain 404 is not what the tree shows for them. Accepted deviation; it belongs to the `unlock_user` measurement the seat filed as #34010.
- N2 (nit) — the header still says `banned` "stays true past `ban_expires` until better-auth clears it at the user's next sign-in". On the kernels this PR newly reaches, `user-session-admission.ts` clears it. The display reasoning is unchanged.
- N3 (nit, outside the diff, follow-up) — two published texts still teach that `ban-user` needs the admin plugin: the `requiresFeature` example in `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` uses `ban_user` with `requiresFeature: admin` ("Hidden entirely when the admin plugin is off"), and the `describe()` of `AuthFamiliesSchema.admin` in `packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts` lists `ban-user` among routes that "answer a plain 404" when the flag is false. `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` already states the opposite. The seat's comment 6897338167 carries this to #34008.
- N4 (nit, prose face) — the `Clause-②:` line in the changeset and the PR body still ends with the dispatch-time clause "the dev measures the gaining kernels and the seat amends if the diff reads otherwise", which will ship in two changelogs. The measurement is done and the answer is `no`. Accepted deviation in the changeset, since a fix there moves the head.
